title: [root] MAX11 loopless k=5 exact decision
description:
## Goal
Decide, exactly, whether MAX_11 lies in the span of the complete loopless degree-five signed-W atom universe (G-0027: 754,017 orbits) plus the 5E/5L carriers. A rational certificate settles the n=11 rung of "two hidden ReLU layers compute max of n numbers" (known n<=10, Rueß et al. arXiv:2607.21651). A negative is a bounded null with a rational separator, routing to enlargement (loops, non-braid generators, degree 6).
## Read first
handoff/2026-09-02-RESUME-SYNTHESIS.md §1 (object), §3 (verified facts), §7/§8a (plan), §10 (glossary). AGENTS.md "Swarm operations".
## Binding rules
See AGENTS.md. Only the orchestrator (AmberBluff) closes beads. Every result names its denominator and its no-claim boundary.

title: Rust column generator for loopless signed-W atoms (validated vs n=9/10 systems + G-0028 prices)
description:
## Context
Path 1 of handoff §7 / step 1 of §8a. A column is the S_n-symmetrised atom function restricted to the sorted cone {x_1<=...<=x_n}: a linear part l in Z^n plus a sparse hinge dictionary h: primitive direction d -> integer coefficient (rows = primitive zero-sum directions with mixed-sign prefix sums, oriented first-nonzero-positive). Two existing implementations disagree only by convention:
- Python `handoff/2026-09-02-amberbluff/probes/loopless_probe_par.py::column_dp` (simple loop-free pairs (A,B); rows d = other-base over sorted joint prefix vectors; nonpositive-on-cone rows dropped; gcd-normalised). Saved outputs: `handoff/2026-09-02-amberbluff/systems/loopless_system_n9.jsonl.gz` (10,976 templates) and `_n10.jsonl.gz` (12,248); one JSON line per template with A,B,linear,hinges.
- Rust `artifacts/math/G-0028/src/main.rs`: for a signed-W record (W=B-A multigraph), w_r(pi)=sum_{t<r} W[v_r,v_t], orientation first-nonzero-positive, ReLU(-z)=ReLU(z)-z folded into the linear part, 10*r*9! base term; it PRICES against a dual and does not emit columns. Universe file: `artifacts/math/G-0027/loopless_signed_degree5_universe_v1.json.gz` (754,017 records; schema in G-0028 README and LOOP_INCLUSIVE_SIGNED_W_SCHEMA.md). Carriers 5E/5L: G-0040 README.
## Outcome
`tools/colgen/` Rust crate: for any loopless signed-W record and any n, emit the full sparse column (l, h) exactly over Z (checked arithmetic) and mod p, streaming (JSONL or compact binary), multi-threaded, designed so loop records can be added later. Also emit, over the whole n=11 universe, the count of distinct retained hinge directions (union of supports) and total nnz.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Positive 1: for every n=9 and n=10 saved template (mapped to W=B-A) the Rust column equals the saved Python column after a documented convention map; report matches/total. Any residual disagreement must be explained by an exact identity and reconciled, not waved through.
- [ ] Positive 2: dual·column over the G-0028 registered records reproduces the frozen G-0028 per-record prices at both primes (or a stated large random sample of the 754,017 scan if per-record prices are stored). State exactly which control was possible.
- [ ] Positive 3: brute-force S_n enumeration (all n! orderings) agrees for all records at n<=7.
- [ ] Planted negative: a single flipped sign in W must change the column and must be caught by the validation harness (show the failing run).
- [ ] Benchmark: per-column time at n=11 on 1,000 random universe records, retained-hinge count distribution, extrapolated total nnz and wall time on 16 cores.
- No-claim: column generation only; nothing about MAX_11 membership.
## Deliverable
`tools/colgen/` + `artifacts/math/colgen-rust/RESULT.md` (commands, input hashes, counts, timings, what was not verified).
close_reason: Verified by AmberBluff 2026-09-02: re-executed validate-templates on n=9 with the committed binary (SHA 32620edc..., PASS 10,976/10,976 exact sparse matches, 28 s) and the --mutate-one-sign planted negative (exit 1, no report). RESULT reports n=10 12,248/12,248, literal n! matches at n=5,6,7, and G-0028 registered price replay 13,419/13,419 with both frozen residue-vector hashes matching (not re-run by me; 600 s). Residual: the planted negative is a schema-level mutant caught before column generation, not a value-level column mismatch; bead .3 must include a value-level negative. No MAX11 claim.

title: Exact rational witness recovery for n=9,10 + exact verifier + upstream translator
description:
## Context
No exact rational witness has been produced by our pipeline at any n; mod-p membership (n=5..10, handoff §3) is not a certificate. The n=11 decision needs an exact-Q lift and an exact full-row verifier, both tested on known answers first (handoff §8a step 1).
Saved systems: `handoff/2026-09-02-amberbluff/systems/loopless_system_n9.jsonl.gz` (10,976 cols, 6,326 hinge rows + 9 linear rows, rank 1,506 mod p) and `_n10.jsonl.gz` (12,248 cols, 16,709 + 10 rows, rank 2,166). Target: linear part = e_n (max coordinate on the sorted cone), all hinge rows = 0. Upstream certificates and verifier: `literature/repos/max-relu-certificates/` (certificate_9_4.json: 337 terms; certificate_10_4.json: 402 terms, lcm denominator 304,819,200; verify_certificate.py conventions in handoff §3).
## Outcome
`tools/exactlift/`: (1) given a sparse integer system consistent mod p, pick pivot columns from the mod-p echelon, solve the r×r system exactly (Dixon p-adic lifting + rational reconstruction, or fraction-free), output a small-support rational solution; (2) an exact verifier over Q: sum λ_c l_c = e_n and sum λ_c h_c = 0 on every direction in the union of supports; (3) a translator to the upstream certificate JSON format so the pinned upstream verifier can be run as an independent check.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Positive: exact rational witnesses for n=9 and n=10 from the saved systems, passing both our verifier and the upstream verifier; report support size, lcm denominator and its prime factorisation (Averkov–Hojny–Merkert Thm 2 forces 2 | denominator for n>=5 and 3 | denominator for n>=10; check).
- [ ] Known-answer: the upstream n=9 and n=10 certificates translated into our column basis PASS our verifier; the upstream n=10 certificate with one coefficient perturbed FAILS (planted negative, show the run).
- [ ] Planted negative 2: the n=9 subfamily with both sides spanning trees (beta=0) is reported INCONSISTENT (campaign G-0007: rank 360 vs 361); the pipeline must not manufacture a witness there.
- [ ] Timing: exact solve time at r=2,166; extrapolation to r≈30k–40k with memory estimate; say whether it fits in 60 GB and if not what the fallback is (e.g. multi-modular CRT with more primes).
- No-claim: nothing about n=11.
## Deliverable
`tools/exactlift/` + `artifacts/math/exact-witness-n9-n10/RESULT.md` + the two witness files with SHA-256.
close_reason: Verified by AmberBluff 2026-09-02: re-ran tools/exactlift verify (script SHA cce46897...) on recovered_n10_witness.json: PASS, 16,719/16,719 rows exact, support 424, lcm 304,819,200; mutated upstream n=10 witness: FAIL with 9 nonzero linear residual rows; unit tests 3/3. RESULT also reports n=9 PASS (415 support, lcm 326,592,000), upstream CLI PASS on recovered n=9, six-worker upstream wrapper PASS on recovered n=10 (not re-run by me; 28 min), and n=9 tree subfamily INCONSISTENT 360 vs 361. Scale boundary honestly stated: dense Dixon does not fit at r>=30k; bead .8 must benchmark the multi-modular fallback. No MAX11 claim.

title: Streaming sketched modular rank engine, validated on n=10 member and n=9 tree non-member
description:
## Context
The n=11 loopless system is ~754k columns × O(10^5–10^6) rows, ~5e9 nonzeros; a dense matrix is impossible (handoff §6 item 6). Plan: stream columns from tools/colgen through two independent sparse random row sketches (direction -> bucket via hash, random ±1 coefficients, m buckets each), maintain a dense echelon basis mod p (rank-sized, blocked reduction), report rank(SA), rank([SA|Sb]), saturation (rank vs m), throughput, peak RSS. Expected n=11 rank 25k–40k (ceiling 160k).
## Outcome
`tools/streamrank/` Rust engine, validated on known answers, with a written resource plan for the n=11 run (m, primes, cores, RAM, wall time).
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Positive: on n=10 (columns from tools/colgen or the saved Python system) with m >= 3×2,166, both sketches give rank 2,166 and MEMBER at primes 1,000,003 and 1,000,033, agreeing with the full dense rank.
- [ ] Planted negative: the n=9 beta=0 spanning-tree subfamily is NON-MEMBER (rank r vs r+1) under the sketch, as it is under full rank (G-0007).
- [ ] Sketch honesty: show a case where m is too small (m < rank) and the engine reports saturation rather than a verdict.
- [ ] Throughput: columns/s and entry-ops/s at n=10; projected n=11 wall time and RAM at m=96k and m=128k; a go/no-go for this 16-core/62 GB box vs a rented node.
- No-claim: mod-p sketched rank equality is neither exact consistency nor a certificate; the exact leg is tools/exactlift.
## Deliverable
`tools/streamrank/` + `artifacts/math/stream-rank-engine/RESULT.md`.

title: EXP-0036: decide MAX11 in the complete loopless k=5 universe + 5E/5L at two primes, exact lift or separator
description:
## Context
EXP-0036 (handoff §9 item 3): the decisive open experiment, gap G-0014. Subject: G-0027 universe (754,017 loopless signed-W orbits) + carriers 5E and 5L (G-0040). Rows: every primitive ambiguous direction touched by any column (d_0 = 0 automatically for loopless atoms) + the 11 linear coordinates. Primes 1,000,003 and 1,000,033. Sketch size from stream-rank-engine's plan with saturation check. Orchestrator writes the preregistration before the run starts; do not start before it exists in this bead's comments.
## Outcome
Either (A) MEMBER at both primes -> pivot support -> exact rational lift (tools/exactlift) -> exact verification on all rows -> upstream-format certificate -> hand to orchestrator for T2 referee; or (B) NON-MEMBER -> rational separator (left-kernel vector lifted to Q) verified exactly against every column (the honest null artifact) -> hand to orchestrator.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Both primes agree on rank(SA), rank([SA|Sb]) and verdict; both sketches unsaturated.
- [ ] (A) exact witness passes tools/exactlift verifier and the upstream verifier; support size and denominators reported. (B) exact separator vanishes on every column and is nonzero on the target, verified over Q.
- [ ] Known-answer gates re-run in the same session: n=10 loop-free MEMBER, n=9 beta=0 NON-MEMBER.
- No-claim: (B) says nothing about MAX_11 in ReLU_2 (both construction papers and G-0084/G-0110 show the loopless k=5 family is not complete).
## Deliverable
`artifacts/math/n11-loopless-decision/RESULT.md` + witness or separator files with SHA-256.

comments.author: AmberBluff
comments.text:
EXP-0036 PREREGISTRATION (AmberBluff, 2026-09-02, written before any n=11 run). Family: max11-loopless-k5-complete-target-aware-solve-v1.
SUBJECT: all 754,017 G-0027 loopless signed-W orbits (loopless_signed_degree5_universe_v1.json.gz, SHA-256 8cbb6a9f...) plus carriers 5E and 5L as defined in G-0040; columns from tools/colgen at a pinned commit.
ROWS: every primitive ambiguous direction touched by any subject column (union of supports) plus the 11 linear coordinates. TARGET: linear part e_11, all hinges zero.
PRIMES: 1,000,003 and 1,000,033. SKETCHES: two independent sparse random row sketches with recorded seeds; m = max(96,000, 3 x the n=11 rank estimate from the stream engine pilot). SATURATION RULE: a verdict is reported only if rank(SA) <= m - 1,000 at both sketches and both primes; otherwise report SATURATED (no verdict) and double m.
DECISION RULE: MEMBER iff rank([SA|Sb]) = rank(SA) at both primes and both sketches; NON-MEMBER iff rank([SA|Sb]) = rank(SA) + 1 at both primes and both sketches; anything else is INCONCLUSIVE and is reported as such, never resolved by choosing.
EXACT LEG: MEMBER -> pivot support -> exact rational lift (tools/exactlift) -> exact verification on ALL rows in the union of supports -> translated certificate through the upstream verifier. NON-MEMBER -> left-kernel vector at both primes -> rational reconstruction -> exact check that the separator vanishes on all 754,019 columns and is nonzero on the target.
KNOWN-ANSWER GATES (same code, same session, before the n=11 verdict): n=10 loop-free saved system MEMBER at rank 2,166; n=9 beta=0 spanning-tree subfamily NON-MEMBER (rank r vs r+1, G-0007). PLANTED CONTROLS: one flipped sign in one column must be caught by the column validator; a perturbed exact witness must FAIL the exact verifier.
RESOURCES: this box only, at most 14 cores and 50 GB; if the pilot projects more than 48 h or more than 50 GB, stop and ask AmberBluff to request a node (human approval required).
NO-CLAIM: NON-MEMBER is a bounded null on the loopless k=5 family and says nothing about MAX_11 in ReLU_2 (G-0084, G-0110, both construction papers). MEMBER settles the n=11 rung only after the exact verification and a T2 referee.
MULTIPLICITY: exactly one preregistered run per prime pair; any parameter change after seeing results is a new arm and is recorded as such.

comments.author: AmberBluff
comments.text: PREREG AMENDMENT 1 (AmberBluff, 2026-09-02 15:40 UTC, before any n=11 verdict; arms declared in advance). Bead .7 (two primes, n=9 and n=10): the sub-family {s = k, beta <= 1} contains MAX_n at both arities (rank=aug 1,152/1,506 at n=9; 1,807/2,166 at n=10) while not carrying the full span; at n=11 it has 120,946 of 754,017 records (6.2x cheaper). {s = k, beta <= 2} (355,166 records) is also MEMBER at both. So EXP-0036 runs in preregistered STAGES, each with the same two primes, two sketches, saturation rule and exact leg as comment 1: STAGE A = G-0027 records with s = 5 and beta <= 1, plus carriers 5E and 5L. MEMBER at stage A -> exact lift -> verification -> done (a stage-A certificate is a certificate for the full family). NON-MEMBER at stage A -> exact rational separator y_A on real rows -> STAGE B = stage-A basis plus every remaining record whose column is not annihilated by y_A (found by pricing all 754,017 columns in one colgen pass) -> rank/verdict; if stage B's verdict is NON-MEMBER, its separator y_B is checked against ALL 754,019 columns exactly; only that all-column check constitutes the loopless-family null. Any record whose column IS annihilated by y_A but is outside span(stage A) is not lost: y_B is recomputed on the enlarged basis and the all-column check is what certifies. Multiplicity: stage A and stage B are two arms of one preregistered experiment; no other subfamily is run first without a further dated amendment.

Host memory is 12-23 GB free with other users' sessions resident, so stage A runs with m = 64,000 buckets per sketch instead of 96,000 (basis at the rank gate 45,000 = 11.5 GB per sketch). Validity is protected by the unchanged saturation rule (a verdict requires rank <= m - 1,000 at BOTH independent sketches and both primes; otherwise SATURATED, no verdict) and by the abort gates (rank > 45,000 or process high-water RSS > 18 GiB = stop, report, request a node). Sketches run sequentially (seed 2026090201 first, then 2026090202), primes sequentially (1,000,003 then 1,000,033). 5L carrier appended as an explicit linear column (eleven coefficients 18,144,000 = 5*9!*... as implemented by --include-five-l), 5E is G-0027 record 0. title: Span structure n=5..10: exact kernels, local-move generation, vertex-collapse lemma, Burnside checks
description:
## Context
Path 4 of handoff §7: the loop-free column families are massively redundant (nullity 267/290/9,470/10,082 at n=7/8/9/10 vs ranks 90/140/1,506/2,166). Understanding the relations could collapse the n=11 solve from 754k columns to O(rank) generators and is the only route toward an all-n theorem. Saved systems: `handoff/2026-09-02-amberbluff/systems/*.jsonl.gz` (n=9,10); n<=8 regenerable in seconds with `handoff/2026-09-02-amberbluff/probes/loopless_probe_par.py`.
## Questions (answer each with computation or proof; a checked negative is a result)
1. Compute exact (over Q, not just mod p) right-kernel bases at n=7,8 (and n=9 if feasible). Are the relations generated by local moves on signed graphs (single edge swap, degree-preserving rewiring, common-edge cancellation)? Measure: dimension of the span of candidate local-move relations vs full nullity.
2. Vertex-collapse candidate lemma (unverified, from a Fable synthesis): "every loop-free n-template column equals the sum over the n labels v of the loop-inclusive (n-1)-template column obtained by placing v at the minimum". State it precisely in the sorted-cone convention, then prove it or give an explicit counterexample at n=6 or 7 (extend column_dp to loops = diagonal pairs (i,i)).
3. Verify or refute the Burnside counts 490,480 (n=12, k=5 loop-free simple pairs) and 18,436,223 (n=11, degree 6) using `handoff/2026-09-02-amberbluff/probes/count_simple_pairs.py` as the reference implementation.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each question has a RESULT section with exact commands, numbers with denominators, and PROVED / REFUTED (counterexample file) / OPEN (what was tried).
- [ ] Any proof is written out and machine-checked on n<=8 by explicit computation.
- No-claim: nothing here decides n=11 by itself.
## Deliverable
`artifacts/math/span-structure-n5-n10/RESULT.md` + scripts.
close_reason: Verified by AmberBluff 2026-09-02: re-executed verify_outputs.py (26 s, all-permutations recomputation of 357/357 n=7 and 430/430 n=8 templates); kernel bases 267/267 and 290/290 replayed over Q, +1 mutations rejected, counterexample exclusions passed; vertex-collapse lemma proof read and accepted (831/831 machine checks); Burnside 490,480 and 18,436,223 reproduced. Bounded: n=9 exact-Q rank left OPEN by the author; local-move refutation is for the named two-term/quadratic families only.

title: Refute track: verify or refute the Safran-derived 25-neuron 3-cover necessary condition
description:
## Context
Path 5 of handoff §7 (refute track, <=15% budget). A lower-bound reader derived, from Safran arXiv:2601.01417 (Prop A.4 and §2.4), that any two-hidden-layer ReLU representation of MAX_11 needs at least 25 first-layer neurons whose supports (size 2–3) form a 3-cover of all C(11,3)=165 triples. This is UNVERIFIED. Paper text: literature/papers/2601.01417*.txt.
## Task
Reconstruct the argument from the paper. Either prove the condition (state it exactly, with the argument written out) or show where the derivation fails. Planted positive: check that the n=5..10 upstream certificates (literature/repos/max-relu-certificates) satisfy the analogous condition at their n. If the condition holds it is a WALL (a necessary condition on any witness, usable as a hard constraint in witness search), never an impossibility result.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Written derivation with locators into the paper, verdict PROVED / REFUTED / OPEN.
- [ ] Certificate check script + table for n=5..10.
- No-claim: a necessary condition is not a lower bound on depth.
## Deliverable
`artifacts/math/refute-3cover/RESULT.md`.

title: Stratified span at n=9,10: smallest natural sub-family carrying the full loop-free span (cheaper n=11 first experiment)
description:
## Context
The n=11 solve costs ~10 h of column generation per pass at 6 threads (colgen benchmark: 0.29 s/column, ~31.7k nnz/column, 754,017 columns) plus ~1 day of sketched elimination per prime. Any sub-universe that provably carries the whole loop-free span at n=9 and n=10 is a 5–10x cheaper first experiment at n=11 with a built-in known-answer check. G-0027's census stratifies the 754,017 n=11 records by cancelled mass s, components and cycle rank beta (trees 12,459; beta=1 44,231; beta=2 22,964; beta=3 2,629; beta=4 64 at s=5). Saved systems: handoff/2026-09-02-amberbluff/systems/*.jsonl.gz (loop-free simple pairs; map to W=B-A and compute s, components, beta of W). Tools: python-flint nmod_mat rank (n=10 full rank took ~200 s), pynauty.
## Questions
1. At n=9 and n=10, for the natural strata of W (by s, by beta, by #components, by max multiplicity, and cumulative unions ordered by size), compute mod-p rank (primes 1,000,003 and 1,000,033) of each cumulative union and of the full family. Which is the smallest natural sub-family whose span equals the full loop-free span? Does that sub-family's span contain MAX_n (rank([A|b]) = rank(A))? Report the ratio (sub-family size / full size) at n=9, n=10, and the corresponding n=11 record count from G-0027's census.
2. Same question for the "collapse" structure: does the sub-family of templates whose W is connected (one component) span everything?
3. Report the rank growth per stratum so the n=11 rank can be predicted stratum by stratum (state the extrapolation rule and its denominator).
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A table per n with stratum sizes, cumulative ranks at both primes, and MEMBER/NON-MEMBER of MAX_n for each cumulative union.
- [ ] Known-answer: full family rank equals 1,506 (n=9) and 2,166 (n=10); trees-only at n=9 is NON-MEMBER (G-0007).
- [ ] Planted negative: one deliberately mislabeled stratum assignment must be caught by a consistency check (sizes sum to the family size).
- No-claim: nothing here decides n=11; a spanning sub-family at n<=10 is a hypothesis for n=11, to be checked by rank equality there.
## Deliverable
artifacts/math/strata-span-n9-n10/RESULT.md + scripts + JSON tables.
close_reason: Verified by AmberBluff 2026-09-02: re-ran verify_outputs.py (PASS: inputs, W collapse, censuses, 4/4 partition mutants rejected, cross-prime agreement; it does not replay modular ranks) AND independently replayed the decision-relevant claim with my own code (python-flint): s=k, beta<=1 sub-family is MEMBER at n=9 (3,496 templates, rank 1,152) and n=10 (4,484 templates, rank 1,807) at primes 1,000,003 and 1,000,033, matching the RESULT. Literal-rule table superseded by the k-relative table in commit 0e9ed29. No n=11 claim.

title: Exact leg at n=11 scale: lift from sketched pivot support, rational separator leg, r>=20k timing, n=10 end-to-end
description:
## Context
Bead .2 proved the exact leg at n=9/10 (support 415/424, Dixon solve 4 s / 11 s, full modular rref 54 s / 228 s). At n=11 the stream engine (bead .3) will decide membership on SKETCHED rows and return a pivot column set S with |S| = r ~ 25k–40k. The exact leg must then work from S alone: gather the exact columns of S (tools/colgen, ~31.7k nnz each), select r independent REAL rows among their union of supports, solve the r x r system exactly (Dixon + rational reconstruction; dense r x r mod p LU at r=35k is ~1.4e13 ops, ~10 GB), and verify the witness on EVERY row of the union of supports of ALL 754,019 columns (a witness supported on S must still vanish on hinges of S's columns only, so verification touches only S's rows — state and prove this). The NON-MEMBER leg needs the dual: a left-kernel vector y of the sketched system at both primes, lifted to Q, with the exact check y·column = 0 for all 754,019 columns and y·target != 0; note y lives on sketch buckets, so the exact separator is y composed with the sketch (a rational functional on real rows). Both legs must be exercised end-to-end on n=10 with a sketched decision before n=11.
## Outcome
tools/exactlift extended: (a) `lift-from-support` taking S + exact columns; (b) `separator` producing and verifying a rational separator from sketch left-kernel vectors; (c) scale test at r = 20k–40k (synthetic full-rank sparse system with known rational solution is acceptable for timing; state it as synthetic) with time and RSS; (d) end-to-end n=10 run with a random sketch of size 3 x 2,166: sketch -> pivots -> exact lift -> verify; and the n=9 beta=0 tree subfamily -> NON-MEMBER -> exact separator verified on all 12,459-orbit... (use the n=9 tree templates from the saved system).
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] n=10 end-to-end from sketched pivots reproduces an exact witness that passes the full-row verifier and the upstream verifier.
- [ ] n=9 trees: exact rational separator verified on every tree column and nonzero on the target.
- [ ] Planted negative: a witness with one coefficient perturbed FAILS; a separator with one entry perturbed FAILS the all-columns check.
- [ ] Scale: measured time and peak RSS for the exact solve at r >= 20,000; projected r = 35,000 and 60,000; explicit statement whether it fits in 40 GB on this box.
- No-claim: nothing about n=11 membership.
## Deliverable
tools/exactlift (extended) + artifacts/math/exact-leg-at-scale/RESULT.md.
close_reason: Verified by AmberBluff 2026-09-02: re-ran unit tests (OK), support_lift.py from the n=10 m=6498 pivot report (PASS, lcm 304,819,200, upstream certificate SHA 4bcb155a... byte-identical to bead .2's, 129 s), sketch_separator verify on the n=9 tree separator (739/739 annihilated, target pairing nonzero) and on its +1 mutant (0/739). Gap carried forward to bead .10: the dense exact solve does not fit at r>=35k (projected 90 GiB) and the r=20k timing was synthetic block-diagonal. No MAX11 claim.

title: Do multi-edge loopless W records add span at n=9,10? (sizes the n=11 rank and a 3x cheaper first run)
description:
## Context
The saved n=9/n=10 systems are simple-pair families: every W = B - A has entries in {-1,0,1} (max multiplicity 1). The n=11 G-0027 universe has 243,467 max-multiplicity-1 records out of 754,017; the other 510,550 records (multiplicity 2..5) have NO analogue in any system we have ranked. So (a) the n=11 rank extrapolation from n<=10 is an underestimate if multi-edge W add functions, and (b) if they add nothing at n=9,10, the 243k simple-W columns plausibly carry the whole loopless span at n=11, a 3x cheaper decision with a built-in check. Either answer changes the EXP-0036 plan (sketch size m, column order).
## Task
1. Enumerate the complete loopless signed-W degree-4 universes at n=9 and n=10 (reuse artifacts/math/G-0027/enumerate_signed_loopless.py if it takes n,k; otherwise a pynauty enumerator with the same canonical form; verify counts by a Burnside/orbit cross-check and by recovering the simple-W subset counts 6,197 (n=9) and 7,203 (n=10) from bead .7).
2. Generate columns with tools/colgen (it takes W records at any n; validate the multiplicity-1 subset against the saved simple-pair columns).
3. Compute mod-p ranks at 1,000,003 and 1,000,033: rank(all loopless W) vs rank(simple W only) at n=9 and n=10; MAX_n membership in each; which multiplicity strata add rank.
4. Repeat for n=7,8 exactly over Q if cheap (small).
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Universe counts with a cross-check; simple-W subset reproduces 6,197 / 7,203.
- [ ] Rank table: simple-W, +mult2, +mult3, ..., all; both primes; membership per row.
- [ ] Known-answer: simple-W ranks equal 1,506 and 2,166.
- [ ] Planted negative: a deliberately duplicated record must not raise the rank (idempotence check).
- No-claim: nothing about n=11 membership; a "multi-edge adds nothing at n<=10" outcome is a hypothesis for n=11, to be checked there by rank equality.

title: Exact lift at r~35k: dense mod-p LU + sparse Dixon with early-termination reconstruction, dense synthetic control at r=20k
description:
## Context
Bead .8 proved the exact leg end-to-end at n=10 but showed the dense Python/FLINT solve does not fit at r = 35,000 (projected 90 GiB, 14 h) and the r = 20,000 timing was a synthetic block-diagonal system, which says nothing about a dense pivot minor. EXP-0036 (bead .4) cannot deliver a certificate without an exact solve of the r x r pivot minor at r ~ 25k-40k, where each column has ~31.7k integer nonzeros (entries small, |value| <= ~10^3) and the minor is dense after elimination.
Observation to exploit: at n=10 the unique solution on the 2,166 pivot columns had only 424 nonzeros and denominator lcm 3.0e8, i.e. the solution is small even though the Hadamard bound is astronomical. Early-termination rational reconstruction therefore ends Dixon lifting after few iterations when the solution is small, and the cost is dominated by ONE dense mod-p LU/inverse of the minor plus one sparse matvec per lifting step.
## Task
Implement `tools/exactlift` (or a Rust helper) `lift-large`: (1) dense mod-p LU of the r x r pivot minor in u32/u64 storage (r = 35k -> <= 10 GiB), using python-flint nmod_mat or a Rust blocked implementation; (2) Dixon p-adic lifting where each step is a sparse integer matvec (A_S stored as CSC, ~1.1e9 nnz at r=35k, <= 9 GiB) plus dense triangular solves; (3) rational reconstruction attempted every k steps with early termination and a final exact check on all rows of the support union; (4) fallback if the solution is not small: multi-modular solve over enough primes with CRT, one modular matrix resident at a time; (5) exact separator leg at the same scale: left-kernel vector mod p from the LU, lifted the same way.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] n=10 known answer: from the .8 pivot report, `lift-large` reproduces the byte-identical n=10 upstream certificate (SHA-256 4bcb155a...) and passes the exact verifier.
- [ ] Synthetic DENSE control: an r = 20,000 random sparse-column integer matrix (~30k nnz per column, entries in [-1000,1000]) with a planted sparse rational solution (support 500, denominators ~1e8) is recovered exactly; a +1 mutation FAILS. Report LU time, per-iteration time, iterations to reconstruction, peak RSS.
- [ ] Projection to r = 35,000 and 60,000 from the measured r = 20,000 numbers, stated with denominators, and an explicit fits/does-not-fit verdict for 40 GiB on this box.
- [ ] Threads <= 6 while other agents run.
- No-claim: nothing about n=11 membership.

tools/exactlift lift-large + artifacts/math/exact-lift-35k/RESULT.md.

title: Exact all-column pricing of a rational separator over the loopless universe (stage-B selection and family-null certification)
description:
## Context
EXP-0036 is staged (bead .4, comments 1-2). If stage A (120,947 columns) is NON-MEMBER, its exact rational separator y (a functional on real hinge rows + linear rows, produced by tools/exactlift sketch_separator / lift-large) must be priced against ALL 754,019 columns of the loopless universe: columns with y·c != 0 are the stage-B candidates, and the final family null is certified only by an exact all-column check y·c = 0 for every column not in stage B's basis. Column generation costs ~0.28 CPU-s per column (tools/colgen, ~31.7k nnz each); the dot product is negligible, so a full pricing pass is ~10 h at 6 threads and is dominated by colgen. This bead builds that pricing pass so stage B can start the moment stage A finishes.
## Task
`tools/colgen` (or a sibling Rust crate consuming the MCOLGEN1 stream) subcommand `price-universe`: input = a separator file (rational weights on real rows, scaled to a common integer denominator; format from tools/exactlift), the G-0027 universe, optional record-order/subset file, threads; for each column compute the EXACT integer dot product (i128 with overflow check, or big-int fallback) between the scaled separator and the column (hinge part + linear part); output (a) the list of violating record indices with their nonzero prices, (b) counts of annihilated vs violating with the denominator 754,017 (+ carriers), (c) SHA-256 of the full price vector, (d) modular prices at 1,000,003 and 1,000,033 as a cross-check that must agree with the exact prices reduced mod p.
## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Known-answer positive: the n=9 tree separator from bead .8 priced against the full n=9 saved system (10,976 columns) annihilates exactly the 739 tree columns and gives nonzero prices on the columns outside its span (report count); pricing the n=10 saved system with a separator built from a proper sub-family reproduces the sub-family's rank deficit (columns with nonzero price are exactly those outside the sub-family span, checked against a direct rank computation).
- [ ] Planted negative: a separator with one entry perturbed prices the tree columns as nonzero.
- [ ] Modular/exact agreement on every column; overflow never silent.
- [ ] Throughput on 5,000 n=11 universe columns at 6 threads, and projected full-pass wall time.
- No-claim: nothing about n=11 membership.
## Deliverable
tools/colgen price-universe (or tools/priceuniverse) + artifacts/math/price-universe/RESULT.md.
